section_title: BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers
content:
BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers

BERT: Key ContributionsA deep Transformer encoder model pre-trained on large corporaThe key: learning representations based on bidirectional contextWhy? Because both left and right contexts are important to understand the meaning of words.Example #1: we went to the river bank.Example #2: I need to go to bankto make a deposit.Pre-training objectives: (1) masked language modeling + (2) next sentence prediction,State-of-the-art performance (2018) on a large set of sentence-level and token-level tasks.

Masked Language Modelling (MLM)All input tokens participate in bidirectional self-attention BUT only the 15% of tokens sampled for prediction contribute to the training loss.Average cross-entropy loss over these selected positions
Network weights are updated based on average CE loss over the sampled tokens

Masked Language Modelling
ExamplesHe is from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.àHe [MASK]from Kuala [MASK], Malaysia.He went to the store. àHe went to the [MASK].

MLM: Masking Rate and StrategyQ: What is the value of k?–They always use k = 15%.–Too little masking: computationally expensive–Too much masking: not enough context 
Q: How are masked tokens selected?–15% tokens are uniformly sampled–Is it optimal? See span masking (Joshi et al., 2020) –Example: He [MASK]from Kuala [MASK], Malaysia.

MLM: 80-10-10 CorruptionFor the 15% of tokens selected for prediction,–80% of the time, they replace it with [MASK] tokenwent to the storeàwent to the [MASK]–10% of the time, they replace it with a random word in the vocabularywent to the storeàwent to the running–10% of the time, they keep it unchangedwent to the storeàwent to the storeWhy? Because [MASK] tokens are never seen during fine-tuning

Masked Language Modelling

section_title: Fine-tuning BERT: Token-level Tasks“Pretrain once, finetune many times.”
content:
Fine-tuning BERT: Token-level Tasks“Pretrain once, finetune many times.”

For token-level prediction tasks, add a task-specific linear classifier on top of each token’s hidden representation.
Fine-tuning BERT

The bigger, the better!

SummaryBERT is a deep bidirectional Transformer encoder pre-trained using masked language modelling.Bidirectional self-attention allows each token to attend to both its left and right context.BERT popularisedthe large-scale pretrain–then-fine-tune paradigm in NLP.Achieved state-of-the-art performance (2018) across diverse NLU tasks.
